title: Extract request cardinality and context bounds

chunks.text: An extract request accepts between one and ten HTTP URLs. Its optional query is capped at 2000 characters, the optional context budget must stay between 128 and 32000 tokens, and force_refresh defaults to false.

Search requires a non-empty query of at most 2000 characters. The result limit defaults to five and is constrained to one through twenty. The only request modes are bm25 and hybrid; mode may be omitted.

The indexing endpoint accepts explicit HTTP URLs in batches from one through fifty. Each index item can report document identity, content hash, lexical chunk count, vector indexing status, vector chunk count, and independent vector errors.
A crawl request accepts one to ten seed URLs. max_pages defaults to 25 and cannot exceed 100; max_depth defaults to one and is limited to zero through three. same_origin defaults to true.

A search response records both mode_requested and mode_used, plus a degraded boolean and optional degradation_reason. This makes a vector-side fallback observable instead of silently presenting it as an unchanged hybrid execution.

title: Lexical and vector indexing are reported separately

chunks.text: Index results distinguish the primary indexed flag and chunks_indexed from vector_indexed, vector_chunks_indexed, and vector_error. This lets a successful lexical write remain visible even when the optional vector side fails.

The default page request timeout is 10 seconds, the redirect ceiling is five hops, and the maximum HTML payload is 5,000,000 bytes. These settings are independent of OpenSearch and extractor-worker timeouts.
The default response context budget is 3500 approximate tokens. At most three chunks are selected per document by default, while indexing targets chunks around 500 tokens.

The extractor worker defaults to http://extractor-worker:3000 with a 12 second worker timeout. Browser fallback is enabled by default, while the initial page fetch still follows the separate HTTP timeout.
The default Redis URL points at redis://redis:6379/0 and successful extraction cache entries have a default TTL of 21600 seconds, which is six hours. A zero TTL is permitted by configuration.

OpenSearch defaults to http://opensearch:9200 with a 10 second backend timeout and TLS verification enabled. The lexical document and chunk indexes are named supracrawl-documents-v1 and supracrawl-chunks-v1.

Hybrid is the default search mode with dense retrieval enabled. The dense model is intfloat/multilingual-e5-small at 384 dimensions, using query: and passage: prefixes. Reciprocal-rank fusion uses k equal to 60.
Outbound URL validation permits only http and https schemes. URLs containing a username or password component are rejected before networking, as are URLs without a hostname.

title: Local and metadata hostnames are blocked

chunks.text: The URL guard rejects localhost, localhost.localdomain, metadata.google.internal, every hostname ending in .localhost, and hostnames ending in .local. These names are blocked before DNS is trusted.
Literal and resolved addresses are forbidden when they are private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved, or unspecified. A public literal address may pass without DNS resolution.

title: DNS answers must all remain public

chunks.text: For hostnames, SupraCrawl resolves the target using the effective HTTP or HTTPS port. Resolution failure or an empty answer set is rejected, and the hostname is rejected if any returned address is private or otherwise non-routable.

title: Redirects are manually followed and revalidated

chunks.text: The HTTP client disables automatic redirects. For 301, 302, 303, 307, or 308, SupraCrawl requires a Location header, resolves it against the current URL, and loops back through public-URL and robots checks before the next request. The configured redirect cap is enforced.
Successful page fetching accepts only text/html or application/xhtml+xml after stripping content-type parameters and normalizing case. Any other media type is rejected as unsupported.

title: HTML size is checked before and during streaming

chunks.text: If Content-Length is a valid integer above the configured HTML maximum, fetching fails immediately. The response body is also accumulated incrementally and aborted once streamed bytes exceed the same maximum, protecting against missing or false length headers.

HTTP status codes 400 or greater become fetch errors. Network exceptions are converted to FetchError, while unsafe-URL exceptions remain distinct. A redirect without Location and a redirect chain beyond the configured maximum are also fetch failures.

Page requests send the configured crawler User-Agent, prefer text/html and application/xhtml+xml through the Accept header, and advertise gzip and deflate content encoding. Redirect following remains disabled in the HTTP client itself.

title: robots.txt policy is cached by origin

chunks.text: robots.txt decisions are cached per scheme-and-netloc origin. The RobotsPolicy default cache TTL is 3600 seconds, and a still-valid cached parser is reused for can_fetch checks.
When robots.txt returns an HTTP status from 400 through 499, the parser is given an empty ruleset. That represents no disallow rules, so ordinary 4xx robots responses do not fail closed.

title: robots.txt server and network errors fail closed

chunks.text: A robots.txt response of 500 or greater is converted to a ruleset that disallows all paths. Network errors also install Disallow: /, providing conservative fail-closed behavior.
The robots.txt body is limited to 512000 bytes. If streamed content grows past that ceiling, the policy switches to a universal Disallow rule rather than parsing the oversized file.

title: robots.txt redirect processing is separately bounded

chunks.text: The robots policy handles redirects itself with automatic following disabled. It performs at most three loop iterations, revalidates each robots URL as public before requesting it, and falls back to Disallow: / if no usable policy is obtained.

title: Static worker extraction is attempted first

chunks.text: For already-fetched HTML the extractor first calls the worker /extract endpoint with both URL and HTML. A successful worker result is labeled readability and does not mark the document as rendered.
If the extractor worker fails, returns invalid JSON, or produces no usable markdown, SupraCrawl runs Trafilatura locally. That fallback preserves links, tables, and formatting and favors precision.

title: Title and canonical metadata are parsed from HTML

chunks.text: The extractor reads the HTML title and the first link element whose rel tokens contain canonical. A relative canonical href is resolved against the final fetched URL, normalized, and falls back to the final URL if invalid.

title: Extraction quality combines length, ratio, and uniqueness

chunks.text: Quality is clamped to zero through one and combines 55 percent useful-length score, 25 percent markdown-to-source ratio score, and 20 percent unique non-empty line ratio. The result is rounded to four decimal places.

When browser support is enabled, Playwright extraction is considered if static markdown is shorter than min_useful_chars, quality is below 0.35, or a recognized SPA shell such as __next or root is present while quality remains below 0.6.

title: Rendered extraction must beat the static result

chunks.text: A rendered worker result replaces the static extraction only if its quality score is higher or its markdown is longer. The rendered result inherits the previously determined canonical URL and can inherit the static title when needed.

The extraction content hash collapses all whitespace runs to single spaces, trims the normalized markdown, encodes it as UTF-8, and computes SHA-256. Cosmetic whitespace alone therefore does not create a new extraction hash.

Approximate tokens charge Latin-script text at roughly three characters per token, while each non-Latin code point adds one token. Empty text counts as zero, and non-empty estimates are never below one.
Markdown headings from level one through six flush the current chunk and update a hierarchical section path. The heading itself begins the next buffer, preserving structural context for retrieval.

title: Lists and tables get extra structural tolerance

chunks.text: Chunking normally flushes when adding a line would exceed the target character budget. List items and table-like lines beginning with dash, asterisk, or pipe are allowed to preserve structure while the current buffer remains below twice the target.

With a query, chunks are ordered by a deterministic score: heading term matches receive a four-point boost, body occurrences contribute directly, and term density contributes an additional scaled component. Earlier chunk ordinal breaks ties.

title: Context clipping preserves source order in the final output

chunks.text: Selected chunks are admitted until max_chunks or the token budget is reached. A final oversized chunk may be clipped to the remaining budget with an ellipsis, and after relevance selection the returned chunks are sorted back into original ordinal order.

Seeds enter a deque at depth zero. The crawler repeatedly removes from the left and appends newly discovered links at depth plus one, producing bounded breadth-first traversal while a visited set prevents repeated processing.

The crawler origin key consists of lowercased scheme, lowercased hostname, and effective port. Missing ports normalize to 80 for HTTP and 443 for HTTPS, so same_origin filtering distinguishes protocol and non-default port changes.

title: Discovered links are normalized and deduplicated

chunks.text: Only anchor elements with href are considered. Relative links are resolved against the final page URL, non-HTTP schemes are skipped, each candidate is normalized, and duplicate normalized URLs are removed while preserving discovery order.

title: Depth and visited-page budgets bound crawl expansion

chunks.text: The crawl loop stops when its queue empties or the visited set reaches max_pages. A successfully handled page at depth equal to max_depth is recorded but does not enqueue its discovered links.

title: Crawler records unsafe and fetch failures per page

chunks.text: Unsafe URLs and FetchError exceptions become CrawlOutcome records with indexed false and an explanatory error. The crawler continues with other queued pages rather than failing the entire crawl request.

title: Stable document ID hashes the normalized URL

chunks.text: The search store derives document_id by normalizing the URL, encoding that normalized value as UTF-8, and hashing it with SHA-256. Equivalent normalized URL spellings therefore map to the same document identity.

title: Cross-origin canonical URLs cannot seize identity

chunks.text: A canonical URL is used as the indexed identity only when its normalized hostname equals the normalized final page hostname. Invalid or cross-origin canonical values remain provenance while identity falls back to the fetched final URL.

OpenSearchStore maintains an asyncio lock per document ID plus a user count. Operations for one document serialize on that lock, and the lock entry is removed after the final user leaves when it is no longer locked.

title: A missing OpenSearch index is recreated and the request retried

chunks.text: Request wrappers detect HTTP 404 from an index operation, clear the corresponding ready flag, call the index creation routine, and retry the original request. Lexical and vector indexes have separate recovery paths.

title: Vector mapping pins model provenance and exact method

chunks.text: The vector chunk index enables k-NN and stores embedding model and dimension in mapping metadata. The embedding field is a 384-dimensional knn_vector using the Lucene engine, flat method, and cosine similarity, and mapping validation checks those values.

La extracción admite de una a diez URLs; la búsqueda limita la cantidad de resultados entre uno y veinte; la indexación admite hasta cincuenta URLs; y el rastreo acepta hasta diez semillas, cien páginas y profundidad máxima tres.

Antes de acceder a una URL, SupraCrawl exige HTTP o HTTPS, rechaza credenciales incrustadas, nombres locales y direcciones privadas o no enrutable. Si un nombre DNS devuelve aunque sea una dirección prohibida, el destino completo se rechaza.

La política de robots se guarda temporalmente por origen. Un 4xx equivale a reglas vacías, mientras que un 5xx, un error de red o un archivo mayor de 512000 bytes produce Disallow: / para cerrar el acceso.

title: Ruta estática y respaldo con navegador

chunks.text: Primero se intenta Readability en el worker sobre el HTML ya descargado y, si no funciona, Trafilatura. El navegador se considera únicamente cuando el contenido estático es corto o de baja calidad, y reemplaza el resultado solo si mejora calidad o longitud.

Los encabezados mantienen una ruta de sección. Con una consulta, las coincidencias en encabezados pesan más que las del cuerpo; después de elegir fragmentos por relevancia y presupuesto, el resultado vuelve al orden original de los fragmentos.

title: Rastreo BFS con origen y presupuestos

chunks.text: El crawler usa una cola FIFO para recorrido en anchura, evita URLs ya visitadas, respeta max_pages y max_depth, y cuando same_origin está activo compara esquema, host y puerto efectivo antes de encolar enlaces descubiertos.

La búsqueda híbrida usa intfloat/multilingual-e5-small con 384 dimensiones, prefijos query: y passage:, y fusión RRF con k=60. El índice vectorial usa Lucene flat con similitud coseno y conserva metadatos del modelo.

title: Canonical como metadato e identidad restringida

chunks.text: El extractor obtiene el primer rel=canonical y resuelve enlaces relativos. Para la identidad del documento, ese canonical solo sustituye a la URL final cuando ambos host normalizados coinciden; uno de otro dominio queda solo como procedencia.
